*   **Performance:** Achieves superior view synthesis quality over NeRF and state-of-the-art on synthetic Blender benchmarks and comparable performance on real LLFF-NeRF scenes [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method achieves superior view synthesis quality over NeRF and state-of-the-art on synthetic Blender benchmarks and comparable performance on real LLFF-NeRF scenes. Source [S1] explicitly states: 'The approach, named 'NeRF in detail' (NeRF-ID), achieves superior view synthesis quality over NeRF and the state-of-the-art on the synthetic Blender benchmark and on par or better performance on the real LLFF-NeRF scenes.' This matches the claim exactly.

NeRF-ID was introduced in the paper "NeRF in detail: Learning to sample for view synthesis" [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the source passages that the approach is named 'NeRF in detail' (NeRF-ID). It further details that this method introduces a differentiable 'proposer' module to replace the heuristic sampling of vanilla NeRF, allowing for end-to-end training. This aligns perfectly with the claim that NeRF-ID was introduced in the paper 'NeRF in detail: Learning to sample for view synthesis'.

*   **Coarse Samples:** $N_c$ points $t_i$ equally spaced along the ray interval $[0, 1]$ (normalized near to far) [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in the notes and passages that the coarse network is queried on $N_c$ equally spaced samples along the ray. Specifically, the notes mention '$N_c$: Number of equally spaced samples queried from the coarse network' and the passage states '(i) the coarse network is queried on a few, Nc, equally spaced samples along the ray'. Additionally, the proposer input preparation note confirms that positions are 'scalars normalized to [0, 1]'. Thus, all facts in the claim are present in the evidence.

The method was developed to enable end-to-end training of the sampling mechanism, improving scene representations and view synthesis quality [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the method (NeRF-ID) replaces the heuristic coarse-to-fine sampling with a differentiable 'proposer' module. It confirms that this allows for 'end-to-end training of the entire system' (coarse network, proposer, and fine network). Furthermore, the text notes that this approach yields 'better scene representations' and achieves 'superior view synthesis quality' compared to vanilla NeRF.

Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.

*   **Training Instability:** Training the proposer from scratch can be unstable due to lack of supervision [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that training the proposer from scratch can be unstable due to lack of supervision. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly supports this in two places: 1) In the introduction, it states, 'Training the proposal module from scratch can be unstable due to lack of supervision, so an effective pre-training strategy is also put forward.' 2) In Section 2.1, it reiterates, 'simply training the entire network... jointly from scratch sometimes works, but sometimes fails to reach good performance. We hypothesize that this is because the supervision is too weak (just the final color of the rendered ray).' Both statements confirm the instability and attribute it to weak/lack of supervision.
